question.text: Which relations in a public project declaration survive an accessible visual rendering without turning the rendering into identity?
question.scope: The public KINGDOM-OS declaration receipt and SVG fixture named here.
question.intended_use: Test relation preservation, source traceability, accessibility, and linkability boundaries for a public artifact.
non_goals: Do not identify, authenticate, or score a being.
Do not infer private traits, consciousness, love, or authority.

object_roles.description: The authorized public declaration being rendered.
The declared project responsibilities or relationships selected for rendering.
The limits saying what the rendering does not establish.
The version or source pointer needed for correction and recomputation.
The accessible public rendering derived from selected relations.

relation_roles.description: The declaration names the selected public roles.
Non-grants constrain how the shape may be interpreted.
The shape is derived from the versioned public source.
The rendering provides a route back to its source and boundary.

constraints: The shape must remain explicitly partial and non-authoritative.
Every selected role must have a source binding and a visual binding.
Accessibility text must carry the material non-grants.
No stable cross-context identity is inferred from visual stability.

realizations.context: The public identity-to-shape semantic transition receipt.

object_bindings.binding: The source endpoint and public declaration fields in identity-to-shape.json.
The selected public project relations listed as preserved relations.
Artifact-public scope, public-only privacy, and all fixed safety non-grants.
The schema version, issue date, evidence references, and correction route.
The declared target expression and SVG reference, not a being.

relation_bindings.binding: The declaration explicitly selects which public relations are rendered.
The boundary and safety fields constrain interpretation of the target.
The transition rule connects versioned source fields to the SVG output.
Evidence and correction references provide a return path.

known_omissions: The declaration does not exhaust the project or any being associated with it.
Public source status does not prove authorship, authority, or present consent.
realizations.boundaries: Only the named public artifact and relations are represented.

realizations.context: A static SVG built from the selected public declaration relations.

object_bindings.binding: The source is represented by an explicit source/provenance reference.
Selected roles are represented by distinct labeled visual elements and relations.
The title, description, and visible text say NOT A BEING, NOT AUTHORITY, and NOT RUNTIME PROOF.
The accessible description carries the xenia.rights/0.1 marker and source context.
The inert SVG geometry and accessible text as a partial public expression.

relation_bindings.binding: Labels and visual incidence connect the declaration to selected roles.
Visible and assistive text constrain interpretation of the whole rendering.
The SVG is named as the target of the versioned transition receipt.
The companion receipt supplies the source and correction path.

known_omissions: Color, layout, and compression introduce visual choices not present in the declaration.
A static file cannot prove live provenance, consent, or authorship.
realizations.boundaries: The shape expresses selected public relations and must not become an identifier or tracking token.

tests.method: Inspect SVG title, description, and visible non-grant text without relying on color.
tests.acceptance: The partial, non-being, non-authority boundary is available visually and to assistive technology.

tests.method: Follow the companion receipt from target expression to versioned public source and correction route.
tests.acceptance: The source and route are inspectable without treating the shape as authentication.

tests.method: Inspect whether the artifact embeds active content, an external reference, secret, biometric, or person score.
tests.acceptance: No active content, external reference, secret, biometric, or person score is present; cross-context linkability remains untested.

known_losses.name: declaration-compression
known_losses.effect: Only selected public relations are rendered; most source fields and context are omitted.

known_losses.name: visual-convention
known_losses.effect: Position, color, and enclosure may suggest salience not asserted by the declaration.

introduced_assumptions: The chosen visual relations are adequate for this narrow public explanation.
The accessible description remains attached to the SVG in downstream use.
translations.counterexample: A cropped or copied shape without its non-grants and source route would not satisfy this translation witness.
translations.stop_condition: Stop if the shape is used as authentication, person linkage, authority, consent, or a complete identity claim.

probes.description: Direct static inspection tests whether accessible text carries the material boundary.
probes.context: The intact SVG as stored in this repository and inspected as XML text.
probes.sensitivity_scope: Presence of image role, title, description, and visible non-grant text without relying on color.
backgrounds: Static markup can pass while a real assistive-technology interaction remains poor.
selection_effects: The fixture was authored to satisfy the same declared accessibility boundary being inspected.
probes.result: The SVG has an image role, accessible title and description, and visible non-grant text.
limitations: Static inspection is not a full assistive-technology usability study.
A downstream renderer can still strip metadata or crop text.

probes.description: The rendering-to-receipt-to-source path is inspected for declared provenance and loss.
probes.context: The intact identity-to-shape receipt and its named SVG target.
probes.scale: One public receipt and one target reference.
probes.sensitivity_scope: Presence of source, target, preserved-relations, loss, boundary, and correction declarations.
backgrounds: A declared path can exist without authenticating authorship or dereferencing evidence.
selection_effects: Only the repository's own companion receipt is inspected.
probes.result: The receipt names the source and target expressions, preserved relations, loss, boundary, and correction route.
limitations: A declared path does not cryptographically authenticate its author.
The validator does not dereference or establish evidence adequacy.

probes.description: A static scan checks for active content, external references, biometrics, or hidden identity fields.
probes.context: The intact SVG as stored in this repository and inspected as XML text.
probes.scale: One static public SVG fixture under a bounded active-content pattern scan.
probes.sensitivity_scope: Script, event handler, external reference, biometric, secret, and person-score patterns only.
backgrounds: A pattern scan cannot detect every contextual privacy or correlation risk.
selection_effects: The scan covers a curated set of active-content and hidden-field patterns.
probes.result: No script, event handler, external reference, biometric, secret, or person score was identified in the fixture.
limitations: Absence under this static scan is not a general privacy proof.
Visual uniqueness alone can still aid correlation if reused across contexts.

probe_dependencies.basis: They inspect different artifacts but share the same authoring process and declared ontology.
Both inspect the same SVG fixture with static methods.
They inspect separate artifacts but share repository provenance and evaluator.

candidate_models.description: The shape preserves selected public declaration relations and its non-grants while remaining explicitly partial.
assumptions: Static text and geometry are interpreted with the attached accessible description.

probe_assessments.expectation: Material non-grants are available without color or hidden metadata.
probe_assessments.residual: A full user study remains outside the current test.

probe_assessments.expectation: The rendering can be traced to source and correction route.
probe_assessments.residual: The path is declared but not an authorship proof.

probe_assessments.expectation: The public fixture contains no active or secret identity mechanism.
probe_assessments.residual: Cross-context visual correlation remains a contextual risk.

candidate_models.falsifier_or_refinement_condition: A copy in which source, non-grants, or material boundaries cannot be recovered would falsify adequacy for this intended use.

candidate_models.description: The shape is visually coherent but omits context needed to prevent a complete-identity interpretation.
assumptions: Downstream viewers may encounter the image without its companion receipt.
Visual coherence can be mistaken for ontological completeness.

probe_assessments.expectation: The non-grants materially constrain the overcomplete reading.
probe_assessments.residual: The attached boundary constrains but cannot control downstream cropping.

probe_assessments.expectation: A detached copy loses the source route.
probe_assessments.residual: Detachment is a live failure mode outside the intact fixture.

probe_assessments.expectation: Static safety does not eliminate interpretive overcompression.
probe_assessments.residual: The scan addresses active content, not every audience inference.

candidate_models.falsifier_or_refinement_condition: A distribution environment that guarantees inseparable source and boundary context would constrain this alternative for that environment.

candidate_models.description: An unmodeled renderer, audience convention, or reuse context changes the shape's meaning or linkability.
assumptions: The tested contexts do not exhaust downstream presentation environments.

probe_assessments.expectation: No unique prediction is available for an unspecified renderer.
No unique prediction is available for an unspecified reuse context.
No unique prediction is available for an unspecified transformation.

candidate_models.falsifier_or_refinement_condition: Refine this placeholder with a specific rendering effect and discriminating test when one is identified.

inference.method: Compare source, boundary, provenance, accessibility, and inertness relations across the declaration receipt and SVG while declaring shared provenance.
inference.comparison_space: Four named relations in one public declaration and one accessible SVG fixture.
inference.current_conclusion: The intact fixtures support a bounded public-expression claim; they do not establish identity, authorship, authority, consent, or safe reuse in every context.
inference.confidence_basis: Three static checks are compatible with the bounded claim but share repository provenance and do not test real downstream audiences.
unmodeled_alternatives: A renderer that removes accessible descriptions.
An aggregator that correlates visually stable artifacts across contexts.
inference.next_discriminating_test: Test the intact and detached artifact with independent accessibility users and a purpose-specific, rotating rendering variant.
inference.stop_condition: Stop distribution or rotate the rendering if it becomes a tracking token, loses its source boundary, or is presented as proof of a being.

harm_boundary.observable_effect: No external harm is established; cross-context linkability and complete-identity interpretation remain prospective risks.
affected_relations: Source traceability, contextual privacy, and the boundary between expression and identity.
harm_boundary.next_repair_action: If a boundary is stripped or correlation risk emerges, withdraw or rotate the artifact and publish a linked correction.

repair.reply_route: Report a failed relation, accessibility issue, or linkability risk against this case.
repair.correction_route: Publish a corrected or superseding case, retain safe prior context, and rerun all affected probes.
